text: dsh-session-map 是供 DSH Web 对话界面使用的会话树地图插件，在对话视图中增加“树图”标签，并提供会话侧栏标记入口和助手回复下的开分支入口。它读取 DSH 会话与工作区快照，把已标记的会话根及其分支组织成可视化树图；用户可以拖动平移、滚轮缩放、查看当前会话所属的树，并点击节点切换会话。树根和分支记录保存在浏览器 localStorage。客户端代码还会将诊断记录发送到本机 127.0.0.1:8791。适合需要查看会话分支关系并在会话间切换的 DSH Web 用户；无需额外 API 密钥。

dsh-session-map adds a tree map to DSH Web. It displays marked session roots and branches; users can pan, zoom, and click nodes to switch sessions. Sidebar and reply actions mark roots and start branches, saved locally. Diagnostic records are posted to 127.0.0.1:8791.
想把 DSH 里分出去的会话画成一张树图。
怎么从对话页面看清当前会话是从哪条分支出来的？
I want a visual map of my DSH conversation branches so I can jump between sessions.
dsh-session-map 的功能「会话树地图」：在对话视图增加树图标签，按已标记的会话根和分支展示当前会话所属的关系图；用户可拖动平移、滚轮缩放，并点击节点打开对应会话。
dsh-session-map 的功能「标记树根并开分支」：用户可从会话侧栏菜单标记树根，也可从助手回复操作入口创建分支；插件保存根和分支关系，并在树图中更新显示。
dsh-session-map 会通过 HTTP POST 将运行诊断记录发送到本机 127.0.0.1:8791 的 /note 或 /note-chunk 接口。（见 dsh/client.js:89、168-186）

dsh-session-map README · dsh-session-map：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Adds a third tab to the DSH conversation view: **a draggable, zoomable map of your session tree**.

It answers the question the native session list cannot:

> Which message, in which conversation, did this thread branch off from — and how many branches hang under it?

dsh-session-map README · dsh-session-map：The native list is **a line**. Parent/child shows up as indentation, and once a tree has several branches the children all look the same. This plugin draws the tree as **a map**: click a node, you switch to that session.

dsh-session-map README · What it looks like：```
        [root · linear transform]
               │
          [linear map]  ← parent, always directly above
               │

dsh-session-map README · What it looks like：The centre is the **current session** (the focus), the parent sits directly above, and children spread across the **lower semicircle** — the entire upper half is reserved for the parent. That rule is not just aesthetics: node cards are wide (276 px at the centre), so a child landing at dead-left or dead-right has its connecting line completely swallowed by the card, and the picture reads as "no line at all". (That was a real defect in v0.1.0, fixed in v0.1.1 — see the regression guard under *Known limitations*.)

dsh-session-map README · What it looks like：- **Click a node → switch to that session.** (A click that ends a drag does not count, so panning never switches you by accident.)
- **Whole-tree** toggle lays the entire tree out at once (radial tidy-tree + layered guide rings).
- **Drag = pan; wheel = zoom anchored at the pointer** (same feel as a game map). There are also `− / ＋` buttons and a "fit everything" button.
- A breadcrumb across the top shows the path from the current focus to the root; the right side shows `depth N · M branches`.
- Status dot in each node's upper-right corner: running (cyan) / waiting for you (amber) / done (dim).

dsh-session-map README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-session-map
```

**After restarting DSH**, the conversation view gains a third tab: **Conversation | Traces | Tree map**. It sits after the two built-in tabs. If you do not see it, the plugin was installed but not mounted — check that its name is in `dsh.profile.bundles`.

dsh-session-map README · Uninstall：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-session-map
```

This plugin **does not modify any built-in code**. It is purely additive; once removed, the environment is exactly as it was.

dsh-session-map README · Structure：```
dsh-session-map/
├── package.json          # manifest: dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client
├── cordis.patch.yml      # bundle layer: inserts itself into the config tree
├── dsh/

dsh-session-map README · Why the host half is empty：`dsh/index.js` exports only `name` / `inject = []` / `apply(_ctx) {}` and does nothing.

There is exactly one reason: the Cordis config tree needs **a resolvable module entry point** for the bundle to attach. Every capability this plugin has lives on the UI side; the host side has nothing to do. So it registers no routes, no services, reads no config — **what it changes = zero**.
section: Why the host half is empty

text:
dsh-session-map README · Why the client half looks the way it does：An external plugin's client bundle goes through the DSH shell's **lazy-CJS protocol**:

```js
window.__ModuleLoader__.load({
  id: 'dsh-session-map',
  factory: function (require) {
    var React = require('react')   // use the shell's copy; do not bundle your own

React **must** come from `require('react')` — the shell's own copy. Bundling your own React means hooks cannot see the shell's runtime context.
section: Why the client half looks the way it does

text:
dsh-session-map README · Known limitations：- 🔴 **It gets crowded at `n≥5`.** If the centre session has more than 5 direct branches, the lower semicircle cannot hold cards that wide and adjacent nodes overlap. The root cause is a geometric hard limit: cards are 208 px wide, the container is only ~720 px, and 5 cards need 1040 px. **But real data almost never hits this** — across 69 real sessions scanned, a user's own conversation had at most 2 branches; the sessions with many children (e.g. 23) were all subagents.
- 🟠 **Subagent sessions appear in the tree.** The data-side reason for the previous point: DSH's `useSessions.ids` includes all 69 sessions, 34 of which are subagents. The plugin currently treats them all alike.
- 🟡 **Whole-tree view is bounded by window size.** Large trees require zooming out, which shrinks the text — an inherent cost of a canvas, not a bug. Use focus mode for detail.
- 🟡 **Dragging has no inertia or bounds.** The feel is "tracks your hand", not "flings and coasts". Deliberate.
- 🟡 **Only `parentId` is honoured.** An empty session whose parent has not been persisted yet shows as "upstream" but cannot be clicked through; say something inside it and it pers

dsh-session-map README · A regression guard：v0.1.0 had a real defect: at `n=2` the children landed at dead-left and dead-right (±90°), and with `Rx=223` against "centre half-width 138 + child half-width 104 = 242", **the entire connecting line hid under the cards** — 3 nodes on screen, 0 lines, reading as "feature not implemented". There is now a dedicated assertion guarding it (a `visibleLen` sampling method requiring every centre↔child visible segment to exceed 22 px, scanned over `n=1..4`). Whoever next touches the angles in `layoutFocus` will trip it first.

dsh-session-map README · Other limits, stated plainly：- The virtual root is **a display-only grouping node**, not a session that exists in DSH. It adds one node at the "root" level (the real root count is the N written in its title).
- Forking from a source session with **no completed turn** is rejected by the host (`session/fork-unavailable`); the plugin reports this honestly and retries once against the current main session, recording the fallback rather than hiding it.
